A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniSER and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Corresponding methods, results, and relocated appendix material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, in-the-wild results, joint-versus-single-task ablations, and qualitative editing experiments in Tables 2–4 and the figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds all-in-one restoration comparisons, user-study outcomes, and qualitative mask ablations in Tables 5–6 and Figures 11–12.

M1.justification: The DiT/VAE framework, training objective, random masking, strength interpolation, generic-prompt training, and effect-addition procedure remain unchanged. New synthesis and LR-SRD mask descriptions provide additional documentation without establishing an algorithm revision.

E1.justification: The training datasets, eight standard benchmarks, and 39-image in-the-wild evaluation are retained. Rain, water drops, and stains in the new comparisons were already demonstrated in v1 Figure 5. The user study and additional model comparisons assess existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an explicitly evaluated all-in-one comparator category: DiffUIR, Unirestore, and BioIR appear in Table 5 and Figure 11. v1 discussed unified restoration research but did not report these comparisons. Existing specialist and generalist comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Table 5 adds evaluation without benchmark-specific adaptation alongside retained adapted results. Section 11.1 introduces individual human assessments of removal completeness and identity preservation, while Figure 12 adds mask and blur controls. Existing training schedules and metrics remain unchanged; the user study does not specify participant counts or a complete scoring protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds qualitative mask/no-mask and hard/blurred-mask comparisons in Figure 12, testing spatial localization, dense-effect removal, and boundary artifacts. Figure 11 adds comparative examples on previously covered degradations. The joint-task ablation and contrast-map analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same unquantified retry description for generative baselines. Neither reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added user-study percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 are unchanged. Table 5 adds AIO baseline scores and UniSER's zero-shot benchmark results, including PSNR 27.43 on SOTS and 25.13 on WSRD+. Table 6 adds user-study percentages of 97.5%, 97.1%, 94.4%, and 89.2% for flare, haze, shadow, and reflection respectively. These are additional results under newly reported evaluations, with the original scores retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same target-compositing rule, atmospheric rendering model, procedural haze construction, and residual contrast definition. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a roughly 3.8M-pair dataset, unified soft-effect removal, mask and strength controls, strong restoration performance, and zero-shot and effect-generation capabilities. New comparisons support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies HALO's realism as geometric and explains that its flares use physically inspired 2D heuristics responding to 3D light-camera geometry. It also adds explanations of mask guidance for dense effects and Gaussian blurring for boundary continuity. The computational-cost limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: New Section 8 substantially expands HALO and LR-SRD construction details, including Cycles/Flares Wizard, scene and flare mixtures, background compositing, and instance-level shadow masks. v2 announces a dataset-release location but removes v1's code-release pledge and reproducibility statement. Documentation remains inconsistent: Section 8 says 375 HALO scenes while Section 3.1 still says 78, so an actual dataset revision cannot be established.

R1.justification: v2 adds BioIR and DiffUIR references and broader foundation-model, VLM, and multi-task-learning citations. Sections 2.1, 9.2, and 11.1 briefly expand AIO and evaluation positioning, while the existing literature survey and central novelty framing remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and conclusion, adds a project-leader annotation, and revises some terminology. The appendix gains a synthesis section and reorganizes its final material into quantitative results, qualitative results, and ablations. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–6 and Figures 11–12, revises Figure 2's caption, and reflows the appendix. The image content of Figures 1–10 and the structures of Tables 1–4 are retained; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new AIO comparisons address a missing comparator category, and Figure 12 provides more direct support for the mask design, producing a limited overall quality gain. Added synthesis documentation is useful, but conflicting HALO scene counts, an underspecified user study, and removal of the code-release pledge temper the improvement. The dataset-release location documents an intended release, not established availability.
